t: You're looking at the Banqueting House on Whitehall, the grandest and best-known surviving example of a banqueting house, a building made for elaborate entertaining. It is the only large part left of the Palace of Whitehall, where English monarchs lived from 1530 to 1698. It matters in architectural history as the first structure completed in the classical Palladian style, which went on to transform English architecture. It was designed by Inigo Jones, who introduced the classical architecture of Rome and the Italian Renaissance to England, and who also designed the Queen's House and the layout of Covent Garden square.
